title: Spectrum of a ring with all primes maximal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring such that every prime ideal of $A$ is maximal. Then $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], in its Zariski topology, is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected (that is, profinite).

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Every prime $\mathfrak p$ is minimal: if a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ is given, then $\mathfrak q$ is maximal by hypothesis and $\mathfrak p$ is proper, so $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p$. Thus $\mathfrak p$ is minimal over the zero ideal. For $g\in A$ write $D(g)=\{\mathfrak p:g\notin\mathfrak p\}$, which is open by the definition of the Zariski topology.

Fix $g\in A$ and $\mathfrak p\notin D(g)$, so $g\in\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-localization-radical] with $R=A$, $I=0$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p$: its minimality hypothesis is step 1. The extended zero ideal is zero, hence $\sqrt{0}=\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$. In particular $g/1\in\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$ is nilpotent, so $(g/1)^n=0$ for some $n>0$. The fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives an $s\notin\mathfrak p$ with $s g^n=0$. This uses no reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 04MG, first proof via Tag 00EV, lemma-standard-open-containing-maximal-point, for W=D(g); local nilpotence as in Tag 00EU, lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring

proof.text: The element $s$ of step 2 satisfies $\mathfrak p\in D(s)$ and $D(s)\cap D(g)=\varnothing$: a prime $\mathfrak r$ omitting $s$ and $g$ would omit $s g^n$ by primality, although $s g^n=0\in\mathfrak r$. Therefore every point outside $D(g)$ has an open neighbourhood disjoint from $D(g)$. Its complement is open, so every $D(g)$ is closed as well as open.

source.place: Tag 04MG, lemma-ring-with-only-minimal-primes, first proof: (7) implies (8), by the principal-open argument of Tag 00EV, lemma-standard-open-containing-maximal-point

proof.text: For distinct primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$, their underlying ideals differ, so, exchanging them if necessary, choose $g\in\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$. The disjoint open sets $D(g)$ and $X\setminus D(g)$ contain $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ respectively, proving Hausdorffness. If a connected subset $C\subseteq X$ contained two distinct points, the same clopen partition would induce two disjoint nonempty relatively open sets covering $C$, contradicting connectedness. Thus every connected subset has at most one point, which is total disconnectedness.

source.place: Tag 04MG, lemma-ring-with-only-minimal-primes, first proof: clopen standard opens separate distinct primes, proving (2) and (3) directly from (8)

proof.text: By clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is quasi-compact for every commutative ring $A$. Together with step 4 this is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected, exactly the meaning of profinite in the statement. The argument includes the zero ring: its spectrum is empty and all three properties hold.
